run.question: Can you see any issues in recent logs for traffic-manager deployment in namespace app-102b

report.summary: Logs for the traffic-manager Deployment in namespace app-102b contain exactly one issue-level line in the authorized window: an ERROR entry on pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-7pl95 at 2026-11-22T09:56:15Z with message "Memory alert", error "Memory requests above 90%, consider adding more memory", status 501 and request_id "req-a]8f2c1d4" (see cited Loki views). That line is the only non-INFO line and the only status>=500 line among traffic-manager pod logs in the window, and it is also the only "Memory alert" line anywhere in Loki's logs for the whole window. Nothing else in the logs looks broken: the 100 newest access-log lines are /health and /api/v1/* requests with statuses 200/201/204, and pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-7pl95's container stdout shows only normal nginx 1.31.9 startup notices with no error text (23 lines read, no previous container instance). The workload itself is healthy in Kubernetes terms: Deployment traffic-manager (nginx:latest, revision 1) is 3/3 ready and was created at 2026-11-22T09:56:13Z, its three pods started at 09:56:14-09:56:15Z with restartCount 0 and empty lastState, and all pod-related events are Normal (Scheduled, Pulled, Created, Started) with no Unhealthy/BackOff/Evicted/OOMKilled evidence. The memory warning is not corroborated by configuration or node state: the Deployment defines no resource requests or limits (resources {} on both the pod template and the running containers) and the only node, opspilot-m1-control-plane, reports MemoryPressure=False with 32859944Ki allocatable memory. Because Prometheus was unreachable in this Run, container memory usage, OOM events and HTTP error-rate metrics could not be checked, so the truth of the "Memory requests above 90%" claim is unresolved; I therefore treat the log line as an observed application-level alert of unknown accuracy, not as proof of memory exhaustion, and record no root cause object.

claims.text: Loki contains exactly one issue-level log line for traffic-manager pods in namespace app-102b in the authorized window: timestamp 2026-11-22T09:56:15Z, pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-7pl95, container nginx, level ERROR, message "Memory alert", error "Memory requests above 90%, consider adding more memory", status 501, request_id "req-a]8f2c1d4". A query with | json | level != "INFO" returned only this line, and a query with | json | status >= 500 also returned only this line.

The same "Memory alert" line is the only occurrence cluster-wide in the window: a Loki query {namespace=~".+"} |~ "Memory alert" returned one line, the app-102b pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-7pl95 entry.

The 100 newest Loki access-log lines for traffic-manager pods in app-102b (from the three pods traffic-manager-585c5579f6-7pl95, -dr6sn and -nv26x, all at 09:56:15Z) are nginx JSON "HTTP request completed" entries for /health and /api/v1/users|products|orders|inventory with statuses 200, 201 and 204; that query hit its 100-line limit so older lines in the window were not returned.

Container stdout of pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-7pl95 returned 23 lines from /docker-entrypoint.sh and nginx 1.31.9 notices (epoll event method, start worker processes 35-42) between 09:56:15.265Z and 09:56:15.311Z with no error text, and the tool reported no previous container instance for container nginx in that pod.

Deployment traffic-manager in namespace app-102b was created at 2026-11-22T09:56:13Z (generation 1, uid d6679311-9fa4-4261-a47e-9b7ab9ad1a88), which is ~10 seconds before the only error log line and ~11 seconds before the query end of the authorized window.

Traffic-manager currently reports 3 desired, 3 ready, 3 available and 3 updated replicas, image nginx:latest, with conditions Available=True (MinimumReplicasAvailable) and Progressing=True (NewReplicaSetAvailable); its single ReplicaSet traffic-manager-585c5579f6 (created 2026-11-22T09:56:13Z, owned by Deployment traffic-manager) also reports 3/3 ready.

All three traffic-manager pods (traffic-manager-585c5579f6-7pl95, -dr6sn, -nv26x) are Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and empty lastState, container started 09:56:14-09:56:15Z on node opspilot-m1-control-plane, and every container has resources {} (no requests or limits); the Deployment pod template likewise sets no env, no resources and only containerPort 80.

Kubernetes events for this workload in the window are all Normal: Deployment traffic-manager ScalingReplicaSet "Scaled up replica set traffic-manager-585c5579f6 from 0 to 3" at 2026-11-22T09:56:13Z, ReplicaSet traffic-manager-585c5579f6 SuccessfulCreate x3 at 09:56:13Z, and 3 Pod events each of Scheduled, Pulling, Pulled, Created and Started; no Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff or Unhealthy events were returned for the namespace.

Node opspilot-m1-control-plane reports MemoryPressure=False with reason KubeletHasSufficientMemory and "kubelet has sufficient memory available", DiskPressure=False, PIDPressure=False, Ready=True, and 32859944Ki allocatable memory, so the cluster node is not in memory pressure at query time.

Two warning events in the window belong to other namespaces and other services, not to traffic-manager: Endpoints orca "Failed to create endpoint for service app-95/orca: endpoints \"orca\" already exists" at 2026-11-22T09:21:00Z and Endpoints signup-service "Failed to create endpoint for service app-162/signup-service: endpoints \"signup-service\" already exists" at 2026-11-22T09:32:52Z, both before the traffic-manager Deployment existed (09:56:13Z).

Rejected: that traffic-manager was harmed by a failed rollout, crash, OOM or eviction during the window. The Deployment is at revision 1/generation 1 and was simply scaled 0->3 at 09:56:13Z, the ReplicaSet's three SuccessfulCreate events produced the same three running pods, all have restartCount 0 with empty lastState, and no Evicted/OOMKilled/BackOff/Unhealthy pod events or container error logs were observed in the views read.

Hypothesis (unresolved): the single ERROR "Memory alert" / status 501 line from pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-7pl95 is a one-off self-reported application alert emitted at container start, and its claim of memory above 90% is not supported by any configuration or node state I could read - the Deployment and containers set no memory requests or limits and the node reports sufficient memory - so it may be a spurious or synthetic message rather than evidence of real memory exhaustion; container memory series could not be read because Prometheus was unavailable, so its accuracy stays unknown.

Hypothesis (unresolved): the status 501 field in the ERROR line does not correspond to a gateway-level failure of traffic-manager traffic, since no other 5xx-status line exists in the traffic-manager log set for the window and the newest 100 access-log lines are all 200/201/204; the field's meaning is only what the emitted log line states and could not be cross-checked against HTTP metrics because Prometheus was unreachable.

Advisory: re-check the memory claim against metrics once Prometheus is reachable (for example container memory working set and limits for namespace app-102b / pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-7pl95), and consider setting explicit memory requests/limits on the traffic-manager containers so a future "Memory requests above 90%" style alert can be validated; also look up request_id "req-a]8f2c1d4" in the request chain by a human with access to the request context.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable for every metrics call in this Run (get_metric_names twice and execute_prometheus_instant_query('up') returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so container memory usage, kube_pod_container_resource_requests/limits series, restart/OOM counters and HTTP error-rate metrics for traffic-manager could not be checked; the accuracy of the "Memory requests above 90%" message is unknown rather than confirmed or refuted.

The workload is only ~11 seconds old at the end of the authorized window (Deployment created 2026-11-22T09:56:13Z, first logs 2026-11-22T09:56:15Z), so there are no traffic-manager logs at all from 2026-11-21T09:56:24Z through 2026-11-22T09:56:13Z; that period is unknown, not error-free, and the deployment's history before 09:56:13Z could not be examined.

The unrestricted Loki log query for the traffic-manager pods returned exactly its 100-line limit (all lines at 09:56:15Z) and is flagged incomplete, so older lines in the window were not returned by that query; only the error/warn/5xx filtered queries can be treated as covering the whole window, and retention or ingest gaps in Loki remain unknown.

Filtered error/alert/501 reads of the logs of pods traffic-manager-585c5579f6-dr6sn and traffic-manager-585c5579f6-nv26x returned no_data (status not ok), so their stdout was not confirmed to be error-free; a subsequent unrestricted read for those two pods was not performed before collection closed.

Queries for resourcequotas, services, ingresses, networkpolicies and for ConfigMaps containing traffic-manager-related data in namespace app-102b returned no objects (status no_data); no_data cannot establish absence, so whether a quota, Service, Ingress, NetworkPolicy or fault-injecting ConfigMap affects traffic-manager remains unknown.

The ERROR line's status 501 and the memory percentage could not be tied to any configured threshold: traffic-manager sets no memory requests or limits, and no Prometheus series or quota object was readable to compute a 90% figure.

The traffic-manager Deployment's rollout history beyond the live objects could not be read (no change-history integration is available in this Run), so when and why the Deployment was created/scaled to 3 at 09:56:13Z is unknown.
next_steps: When Prometheus is reachable, query container memory working set and limits for namespace app-102b / pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-7pl95 around 2026-11-22T09:56:15Z to validate or refute the "Memory requests above 90%" alert.
Read the full stdout of pods traffic-manager-585c5579f6-dr6sn and traffic-manager-585c5579f6-nv26x to confirm whether any warning text besides the 7pl95 ERROR line exists.

Confirm whether the "Memory alert" line is expected application behaviour (for example an injected/synthetic health message) by inspecting the nginx image or log generator that produced request_id req-a]8f2c1d4.
Decide whether traffic-manager should declare memory requests/limits, since its containers currently declare none, so that memory alerts can be validated against a real limit.
